title: Model task-sync crash, retry and two-host exchange in TLA+
outcome: Model task-sync crash, retry and two-host exchange in TLA+
acceptance: A bounded TLA+ model covers export planning, recorded head, journal, file publication, confirmation, import commit or rollback, crash and retry, expected-tip movement, and two independently writable hosts exchanging through Git fast-forward, merge and non-fast-forward outcomes

The model checks concrete safety invariants: no overwrite of uncommitted local data, no own-export adoption without the exact parent and changed paths, no journal removal before the comparison basis is recorded, no source head for content not imported, no durable dry-run effect, no duplicate imported versions or reminted identities on retry, and explicit conflict rather than silent reset or merge
The model states its bounds and fairness or quiescence assumptions and checks whether retries converge when no new commits arrive; it makes no unbounded always-works claim
An actual TLC run reports the complete spec, configuration, state counts, constraints and results, with retained artifacts and every counterexample minimized and explained

Kimi independently reviews the model against the Rust protocol and checks each reported violation or successful invariant; every actionable counterexample receives a concrete implementation reproduction or regression-test proposal for Sol/Opus
The work changes no production code, adds no gate and does not block or consume the current sync landing's build capacity

completion.summary:
Delivered a bounded TLA+ model of Engram's task-sync folder exchange. It models the Rust candidate dc092ddc (R31; the protocol is equivalent at R34; it does not describe master f5dd92bf). The final spec is v11, sha256 27086bc9f1a301f25fe3d919d2ab1d349f0d64b0d88a93d8d86a354434255c70. TLC ran on DL560 s4 under Opus2 GOs, the final run being round 9 (#3185): 25 configurations.
- Clean: every safety configuration, on the full invariant set and the action properties ExplicitConflict, NoInventedValue, NoReplacedRecord and DryRunHarmless.
- Bounded convergence: Converge and ConvergeBootstrap, under the stated order and fairness assumptions.
- Documented findings F1–F5 (class b) reproduced; each has a filed follow-up (w-2f8a670c3179, w-ba1e43c78db5, w-85c7a24d3520, w-0a11063c9536, w-b7726d27f7e0).
- S1 (class a, Medium) is tracked in w-45fe538db32a.
- Five reachability witnesses and three negative controls (NegReplace, NegReplaceCount, NegSilent) behaved as intended.
- All counterexamples are minimized and explained in the README.
Reviews:
- Kimi's C5 reviews passed (v6–v11).
- Opus and Sol confirmed v11 with no Medium or higher (Fable #38).
- Independent acceptance evaluation (session-19117): all 6 criteria PASS.
After the evaluation, Opus's two README Notes were applied without re-review, as Fable ruled: NoInventedValue is stated for governing planning only, and MergeFirst/F3Min/F4Min/F5Min are marked as PARTIAL checks of ExplicitConflict and NoInventedValue. The final handoff MANIFEST.sha256 is sha256 22325822b82dd266ba98d41a82dbfa68206eca9b265a887c6d09e6ee46c6d05f (the evaluated manifest was 817451b9…e1e0; README.md alone changed).

No production code or tests changed, no gate added, and no sync landing capacity was used.
